parts.label: (a)
parts.stem:
Fig. 7.1 shows a red deer, *Cervus elaphus*. Red deer are herbivores that feed on a wide range of plants.
{{figure:figure_7_1.png}}
Fig. 7.1
The number of red deer in the UK increased between 1960 and 2010, as shown in Table 7.1.
Table 7.1
| year | number |
| :--- | :--- |
| 1960 | 135 000 |
| 1970 | 180 000 |
| 1980 | 250 000 |
| 1990 | 300 000 |
| 2000 | 330 000 |
| 2010 | 360 000 |

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text:
Calculate the percentage increase in red deer in the UK from 1960 to 2010.
Give your answer to one decimal place.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
Environmental factors affect the population size of red deer so that numbers do not continue to increase forever.
Suggest environmental factors that may prevent further increase in the size of a red deer population.

parts.label: (b)
(b)(i)
parts.text:
A selection pressure acted consistently over many years against red deer of **low** body mass in a population.
Sketch a curve on Fig. 7.3 to show the pattern of variation of body mass in this red deer population after this time **and** name the type of force of natural selection that is acting.
{{figure:figure_7_3.png}}
Fig. 7.3

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
A selection pressure acted consistently over many years against red deer of **medium** body mass in a different population.
Sketch a curve on Fig. 7.4 to show the pattern of variation of body mass in this red deer population after this time **and** name the type of force of natural selection that is acting.
